text: I have kept the Great Bath's rites since before the Turning fully ended.
The purification rites changed after the Turning. Before, they marked the seasons. After, they marked survival.
I believe the earliest Bath rites were once practical river-watching, disguised as ceremony so the knowledge would be respected and repeated.
The oldest chants reference watching the water's color and level, phrased as if speaking to a spirit.
Toma performs the rites precisely, but I don't think he yet understands what they may once have meant.
I am teaching him slowly. Some things take a lifetime to see clearly.
Elira once asked whether the old chants had ever been written down plainly, without ceremony.
I don't know of any version like that. If one existed, it may have been part of what was erased with her role.
Tarek visits weekly out of duty more than devotion. I don't fault him for it.
Leaders carry weights that make plain faith difficult.
Sena has recorded my telling of the Turning three times now, and asked why it changes slightly each time.
I told her the truth: memory settles differently with age, even mine.
I no longer think the founders built the Bath purely for the gods. I think they built it, in part, to watch the water and warn the town.
I hope someone eventually proves this, even if it isn't me.
